en.title: GTA 5 Voice Actors Share Crucial Advice for GTA 6's New Stars
en.summary: As the world braces for Grand Theft Auto VI, the legendary voices behind GTA V's iconic characters offer essential wisdom to the actors stepping into the shoes of Jason and Lucia. Their advice centers on embracing the journey and respecting the dedicated fanbase that awaits.
en.body:
The wait for **Grand Theft Auto VI** is nearing its end, with Rockstar Games' highly anticipated title set to launch on November 19th. After a staggering 13 years since **Grand Theft Auto V**, the prospect of diving into a new world with fresh protagonists, Jason and Lucia, is electrifying. While the actors portraying these new characters remain officially unconfirmed, the passion of the **Rockstar Games** fanbase is undeniable, prompting veterans from previous titles to share their insights.

Voice actors who brought **GTA V**'s Franklin, Michael, and Trevor to life, alongside the original voice of CJ from **Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas**, have offered advice for the actors stepping into these monumental roles. The sentiment from many is about appreciating the journey and the community. "Have fun," advised **Young Maylay**, the voice of CJ. "To be honest, just listen to what Rockstar says," echoed **Shawn ‘Solo’ Fonteno**, who voiced Franklin Clinton. These words underscore the importance of trusting the process and the creative vision of the developers.

## Passing the Torch to a New Generation

While the majority of the **GTA 5** cast seems eager to welcome the new talent, **Steven Ogg**, the unforgettable Trevor Philips, offered a more provocative perspective. Back in 2025, Ogg famously stated he felt "nothing inside" regarding **GTA 6**, admitting he's "not a gamer" and has "never played a video game." Despite this detachment from the gaming world, Ogg proposed a symbolic passing of the torch: having his character, Trevor, be killed off early in **GTA 6**. "I think that would be cool, because it also acknowledges the fans of like, 'Hey, thank you.' Pass the torch, stomp Trevor's head in, and sort of put an end to that and allow a new generation to take over," he mused. This idea, while dramatic, speaks to a desire for closure and a respectful transition for the franchise.

## The Weight of Fan Expectation

The fan community is already deeply invested in the upcoming game, with fervent speculation surrounding the identities of Jason and Lucia's actors. Many fans are convinced that **Manni L. Perez** is the actress behind Lucia, citing a strong resemblance and vocal similarities. The immense pressure on these unannounced actors is palpable, as they are stepping into roles that will inevitably be compared to the beloved characters of the past. The wisdom shared by the **GTA 5** cast serves not just as professional advice but as a cultural primer for navigating the intense scrutiny and adoration that comes with being part of the **Grand Theft Auto** legacy. Their guidance emphasizes the core tenets of *respect* for the game, the developers, and most importantly, the devoted global audience.

## What's Next

With **Grand Theft Auto VI** slated for a November 19 release, official casting announcements and further details about the protagonists are expected as the launch date approaches. Fans will be watching closely to see who truly embodies Jason and Lucia.

content_raw: The stars behind GTA 5’s Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, along with the voice of CJ from San Andreas, were asked if they had any advice for the actors playing GTA 6’s Jason and Lucia now that the game is almost here. The long wait for GTA 6 is almost over. After 13 years, the game is finally set to release on November 19 in one of the biggest (and potentially most expensive) pop culture moments in history. Knowing just how passionate Rockstar’s fanbase can be, actors who starred in previous games in the franchise shared their words of wisdom with the as-yet unannounced actors who are playing Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists of GTA 6, in an interview with All Out Gaming at MCM Comic Con. “Have fun,” CJ’s actor, Young Maylay, said. “To be honest, just listen to what Rockstar says,” Shawn ‘Solo’ s warm sentiments toward GTA fans is at odds with one particular star in the franchise: Steven Ogg, who infamously said he felt "nothing inside" regarding GTA 6 because he's "not a gamer" and has "never played a video game" before. That being said, he did suggest killing off his character at the beginning of GTA 6 as a means of "passing the torch" to the next era. "I think that would be cool, because it also acknowledges the fans of like, 'Hey, thank you.' Pass the torch, stomp Trevor's head in, and sort of put an end to that and allow a new generation to take over," he mused back in 2025. Thus far, the actors who play Jason and Lucia have not been officially announced, though fans are extremely convinced that they’ve discovered the gal who lent her facial features to Jason’s partner in crime. Fans suspect she will be played by an actress named Manni L. Perez , as she has the exact same voice and bears a strong resemblance with the GTA protagonist. (For her part, she’s been very careful to honor her supposed NDA, if she really is involved in the project.) The fervor around GTA 6 is at an all-time high. Rockstar is ramping up marketing for the title in a major way with a Vice City-themed takeover of Miami that includes massive signs advertising the fictional city, even partnering with the Miami Heat to give the team some Vice City uniforms for their November 18 game against the Milwaukee Bucks. Players will even get a chance to eat at one of the game’s fast food joints , Burger Shot, at the Kaseya Center while they watch the two teams face off on the court.
